text.p: Following are some of the major events to have occurred on July 16 in history.
622 - This date is generally considered as the start of the Islamic Era when Mohammed began his flight from Mecca to Medina.
1048 - Benedict IX, known as the "Boy Pope", resigned from the papacy.
1486 - Andrea del Sarto, a Florentine painter of the Renaissance, born.
1557 - Anne of Cleves, fourth wife of King Henry VIII, died; her marriage to the king was annulled after six months.
1661 - The first banknotes in Europe were issued by the Bank of Stockholm.
1858 - Belgian violinist, conductor and composer Eugene Ysaye born. He taught Yehudi Menuhin for a short period.
1867 - Reinforced concrete was first patented by Jospeh Monier of Paris.
1872 - Norwegian explorer Roald Amundsen born. He was the first to reach the South Pole in 1911, a short time before Robert Falcon Scott.
1896 - Trygve Lie, Norwegian statesman and first secretary-general of the United Nations from 1946-52, born.
1907 - U.S. film actress Barbara Stanwyck born; she appeared in films from 1927 including "Double Indemnity".
1911 - U.S. dancer and film actress Ginger Rogers born. She was best known for her partnership with Fred Astaire and appeared with him in "Top Hat" and "Roberta".
1917 - The Bolsheviks began an attempt to seize power in Petrograd but were defeated. Trotsky was arrested and Lenin went into hiding.
1918 - Tsar Nicholas II, the last Russian tsar, was murdered together with his family and entourage by the Bolsheviks at Yekaterinburg.
1935 - The world's first parking meters were installed in Oklahoma city.
1942 - Nearly 14,000 Jewish people were arrested in Paris as part of a German roundup of the Jewish community
1945 - The U.S. staged the first test of a plutonium weapon, codenamed "Trinity", before dawn in the New Mexico desert.
1948 - The world's first turbine-propellor aircraft, the Vickers Viscount, made its maiden flight.
1950 - The largest ever crowd to watch a soccer match, over 199,000, saw Uruguay beat Brazil 2-1 in the World Cup final.
1953 - Hillaire Belloc, French-born British writer, died. He was best known for his nonsensical verse for children.
1965 - A seven-mile tunnel through Mont Blanc connecting France and Italy was opened by General de Gaulle of France and President Saragat of Italy.
1969 - Apollo 11 was launched on its historic mission to land men on the moon with astronauts Neil Armstrong, Buzz Aldrin and Michael Collins aboard.

1989 - Austrian conductor Herbert von Karajan died. He was one of the great conductors of the 20th century, dominating the post-war world of music in the concert hall, opera house and recording studio.
1992 - Vice-President Shankar Dayal Sharma was elected India's ninth President.
1993 - Britain's MI5 security service ended more than 80 years of secrecy when it published a booklet on its operations.
1994 - The first fragments of the Shoemaker-Levy 9 comet hit Jupiter.
1995 - Two Americans, jailed since March for illegally entering Iraq, were released by Saddam Hussein.
1995 - British writer Stephen Spender, one of the great literary names of the 20th century, died.
1996 - Germano Maccari was convicted of being one of two killers who shot former Italian Prime Minister Aldo Moro in 1978.
